utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Karadzic, let's finish your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we discussed the fact that the investigation at Markale started after the killed and the wounded were removed and after a certain degree of intervention on the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to object to that question. The evidence, I think, is that Mr. Sabljica arrived after the killed and the wounded had been removed. The evidence is not that the investigation only started at that point. It concerned the arrival of this particular person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We could understand that, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to what extent the site had been changed before you arrived.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the site was secured by the policemen and the police administration of Stari Grad at the time when we arrived, and the whole place was sealed off. As far as the stalls at the market were concerned, the chaos was complete. Everything was scattered, with bloodstains all over, body parts. I cannot say what it looked like exactly when the shell just fell. I can tell you what it looked like when I arrived: The stalls had been overturned. Everything was on the ground. Body parts, tissue. And the place was sealed off by police tape. It was done by the police administration of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you just arrived, what was the extent of changes to the site that you found?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand your question. What changes? What we found was the state of affairs that we established. Apart from the fact that the bodies of the wounded and dead bodies were removed, everything else was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the only change was that the bodies of people and people were removed. Everything else was the same. When you arrived at the site, did you find the tail fin in the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not straight away. When we approached the site where the shell landed, when we located the crater, we could not see the tail fin in it. We could see a lot on that first footage that we saw. The investigating judge told us then to pay more attention to the place where the shell landed, and I think after clearing the surface layer of tarmac by hand and after the scenes of crime officer removed parts of body tissue and that surface part of the tarmac, we cleared the crater but we still didn't find the -- or take out the tail fin before the arrival of the UNPROFOR, and you could see on the footage that the UNPROFOR officer took out the tail fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He removed the tail fin the day after.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the day when we did the on-site investigation, not the next day. They arrived the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We discussed a little yesterday the distribution of goods and the concentration on the very plateau of the market, and we had no time to present a full picture where the most goods were concentrated and where most of the buyers were thronged.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the people were circulating all over the compound and the market, because people thought the market was safe, relatively safe, being sheltered by surrounding buildings. You know that there was the supermarket UPI there also and some people were selling some goods inside. So it was quite packed. I cannot tell you really that there were more people in the left corner or in the right corner. People were circulating all over the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What were your first steps in that investigation? Probably the description of the site and then certain investigative steps. I suppose the first ones were focused on finding the tail fin and the identifying parts of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all came the analysis of the crater, to apply that basic method I explained to determine the direction, the remnants of the shell, and the remaining procedure was followed with the presence of the investigating judge, I believe Mr. Kandic. The standard procedure that we applied in such instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did it turn out that the tail fin was inside the crater after you seriously cleared the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we measured the depth from the surface of the tarmac until the depth where the tail fin was stuck. We located the peripheral shape scarred traces. That depth was 9 centimetres. It was impossible to use the chalk to draw, because it was rather wet and bloodstained. And we removed the impurities as far as we could, so we used the sticks from our kit to create the standard schematic that we've reviewed over the past few days to determine the azimuth, the direction of descent, to create the documentation and write up our findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In those comprehensive investigating steps, did you also proceed to determine the direction from which the shell came and the angle of descent? Was that also written up?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did determine the direction, but I'm not sure we determined the angle of descent. The direction from which the shell came was established according to the well-known method. It was 18 degrees -- or, rather, 320 mils, approximately, although we didn't have the artillery compass to measure it in mils, but the degree of the angle of descent was 18 degrees. I think it's in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are certain curiosities about Markale that we have to clear up. Did you in your first contact with the site determine the angle of descent?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the first contact. That time we dealt exclusively with the direction from which the shell could have come. Later, expert teams, local and international ones, proceeded to investigate. I had occasion to see some of their reports, and they dealt more with the other elements, including the angle of descent. The most important thing is that we all established that the shell was detonated on impact with the tarmac, and this tail fin was found, which we did not touch until the arrival of the French UNPROFOR battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain that the first contact of the fuse with the hot surface was on the stall, according to some, whereas others say it was upon impact on the hard surface? How can you explain this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that anyone claims it exploded on the stall. I can say with certainty it exploded when it hit the tarmac. Before that, it did not touch any hard surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you then determined the direction from which the shell could have come, you did not establish the angle of descent, and then you proceeded with your investigation the next day -- or, rather, investigation continued the next day.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except I did not come the next day because my part of the job and the job of the late Cavcic was finished at that point at Markale. We continued to work in the lab, writing up a more detailed report, preparing the documentation, et cetera. Other teams came out on the site later, and I was not a member of the teams that continued in the days that followed to deal with the Markale case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come that among you who first came to the site and collected certain evidence were excluded from the follow-up work, although the team still needed a ballistics expert? Was it perhaps that someone did not like what you wrote in your report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the answer to that question. I never asked, and nobody ever answered it. But if you ask about our report and our findings, it is pretty much consistent with the findings of, let's say, an international team of military experts concerning the direction and the deviations in azimuth. I think there was a Major Smith or a colonel, an Irishman, who headed the one team. They used the artillery compass and determined the angle of descent at 360 mils. Now, why teams were engaged that did not include us were engaged, I don't know. I know that one mechanical engineer from the university was engaged. He taught rocket engineering. And there were also experts from the MUP, from the counter-sabotage team, from the bomb squad, and there was also a French colonel part of that team. Now, why we did not continue in the follow-up work, after all, we completed our job in those four hours on the market, what we found was enough for the report that we normally write, including the methods and the tool kit that we had that enabled us to complete our assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This second investigation was led by Mr. Zecevic, a forensic expert, and other forensic experts in his team.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was also a professor at the mechanical engineering faculty, and he was engaged by the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you submit your report and to whom?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We finished our report the very same day, late at night, I believe, around 8.00 p.m., after we returned to our office. We made our report. The photo documentation had already been prepared. The whole file was forwarded to the competent prosecutor's office in Sarajevo, whatever it was called, the court, and the whole case was prepared and an indictment was brought against unidentified persons for murder and grievous bodily injury. It was the usual procedure in view of the number of casualties at Markale. We adhered strictly to the standard procedure of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who established the coordinates in those later reports? You sized up the situation before Zecevic came, and then he showed up on the scene. Who authorises all these findings? Who verifies these findings, both yours and his?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said our findings were sent directly to the prosecutor's office, and his findings were probably included in that case file as additional evidence, but that did not really concern me. I had completed my part of the job, and I was no longer engaged in any way. The first next time I had anything to do with it was to testify against General Galic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up a diagram, ERN 1025-920. 02115 -- 65 ter 10616. Page 4 in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Could we please have on the other half of the screen parallel to this 65 ter number 096 -- 9623. Maybe it's going to be easier this way, if we have two parallel texts on the screen. 65 ter 9623. The first page first, and then page 3. Also, on the other half of the screen 65 ter 10676, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think it's impossible because we have both English and B/C/S version. So it's impossible to show four documents at the same time. Why don't we go one by one. And I would like to tell you that -- to try to conclude your evidence -- your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then do it individually. 65 ter 9623.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This, Your Honours, is Exhibit Number P1440.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then page 3 on this document. This is what I'd like to recommend now: That the health service look into the temperature in this courtroom. I think that in addition to stress, tension, concentration, that the temperature in this room can be a source of health problems. Now page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If this is page 3, please have a look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this diagram. I worked on it together with the forensic technician, Beslic. It is a sketch of the site, a bird's-eye view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are north and south marked?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: North is marked. That is the shorter vector, the shorter arrow. It denotes the north. The other arrow denotes the direction from which the shell came and also the angle, 320 mils or 18 degrees. C is the centre of explosion, and the rest are buildings in the surrounding area. 1, 2 is the supermarket. If you remember that supermarket in Sarajevo, it's still the same. Number 5 is the building known as the 22nd of December, "dvadesetdrugog decembra." I don't know what it's called now. As for these squares, one is number 3. Those are the market stalls. And you have view A down here. You have the dimensions of the stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what all the stalls looked like; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an ideal picture, idealised, if I can put it that way. It doesn't represent the actual situation as it was. It was important to see where the solid objects were. Stalls can be moved; right? So the centre of the explosion is focused on the supermarket building. And if you see there by the market, 1.420 millimetres --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We won't be able to deal with all of Markale with you because you worked only on one part, but the team that you worked with and with whom you exchanged findings, well, could you please try to help us, explain what this space was, and some of your findings and some of Zecevic's commission's findings are identical, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they should be. As for the direction from which the shell came, I'm sure they're identical. The dimensions, the positions of the centre of the explosion that, should be identical, because we use the same measuring bands to this day. There is a memorial plaque there, and for a long time on the asphalt it was marked. I mean the place where the shell fell was still marked by that red substance we talked about yesterday. The memorial plaque is still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to show that the results of findings are the same in a particular investigation, it is best to show the sketch that you signed. 65 ter is 09623, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the sketch. We have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's what we are seeing on the left side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 10676, Zecevic's sketch. Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this Zecevic's diagram of the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't draw it. I've never seen it before. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, it is part of the investigation material, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, we've confirmed that. But Zecevic submitted this later, upon instructions from the court. He was engaged for an additional expertise, to provide an expert opinion. You see that it corresponds the angle of descent, 18 degrees, the position of the crater, and so on. That's how we marked it too. I don't see any difference really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. Can you mark the cardinal points here and also the basic areas -- or, rather, the basic relationships.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's the north, N. I'm just going to put a circle around it. So the south is opposite, and then east and west. The buildings are fixed. You can read it for yourself here what the dimensions are. It's in metres, all the distances. From the edge of the supermarket to the edge of the sidewalk. Again, this is a bird's-eye view, the 22nd of December building. I think that the sketch is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it generally accepted?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a technical sketch, a technical drawing that is part of a documentation which can always assist someone who wants to find the place of explosion, and therefore it can be related to fixed objects and you see where north is and also the direction from which the shell came. As such, it is part of documentation, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us whether axes can be shown on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the longer vector, and that shows the longer axis, because that is actually the direction from which the shell came. And we've dealt with that over these past three or four days. It's already drawn here. If you wish, I'm going to mark it more prominently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that it's clearer for us when we look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is, the direction from which the shell came. It's marked with a V.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see what the orientation is of this part?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. In relation to well-known streets in Sarajevo. That's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This down here is the former Tito Street. It has a new name now. I'm going to put TS here for Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What direction is this street? Blue, perhaps, for these localities.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Tito Street goes from the east to the west. This is it. It's a bit to the south-east in relation to the point of impact. That is Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, do we not have the English translation of this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. I'll have a look for it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, how would we determine the cardinal points here in relation to these elements of the streets and these passageways between the market stalls in relation to this entire layout of the market and the neighbouring streets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's already set. You see here I've drawn it, where the west, where the east is, et cetera. If you wish, Tito Street does not exactly go from east to west. There is a bit of an angle there. So it is south-west towards the north-east in relation to the point of impact on the market. You know that Tito Street is underneath, and it's in the upper right-hand corner by the 22nd of December building that the incident took place, right by the UPI supermarket, if you remember that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The upper right hand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The -- we have an English translation of the key to this diagram, and it's 65 ter number 10676, and it's the last page in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 83.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can first have this drawing admitted, and then we're going to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Sabljica, if you could mark the point of impact of the shell. Vertically it is north-south; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've marked it. Can't you see? North-south. And this is the impact here, impact place. So you see that there is a circle there around the point of explosion, and you have the cardinal points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was in the south-eastern corner of Markale, right, the explosion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on how your you're viewing the Markale Market. If you're viewing it from Tito Street, then it's up in the north-east quadrant if you're standing in Tito Street. Now we are viewing everything in relation to the point of explosion. If you're looking at Markale Market, you're standing on Tito Street; right? The explosion took place in the north-eastern part of the market. That is to say, the upper right-hand corner. So the supermarket is on some steps, and then there's a passageway between the market and the 22nd of December building, there's a bit of a sidewalk, and then the first or second row of the market stalls, that's where the shell fell. Is it a bit clearer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's clear to me, but I'm afraid that if Tito Street is the basis of this photograph -- or, rather, of this drawing, as we're going to see on photographs, then the explosion would have to be on a diagonal on the other end of this same diagonal; right? So if this is the market that we're viewing from Tito Street, then the explosion would have to be in a corner that's opposite to this one. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. I'm going to repeat once again. The 22nd December building stretches to the east in the Markale square. If you go to Titova Street, and the tram starts from the cathedral, there are two butcher shops there and another bakery shop, you turn the corner and you reach the Markale. You can enter it from that side or you can enter it from the upper side. So normally you have people there, vendors with boxes on this corner because there's no traffic there except for delivery vans for the supermarket. So that would be in the right-hand corner of Markale if viewed from this street. So I'm talking about Markale I. That's how we used to call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to correct my earlier reference. It's P1440, and it's page 6 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you change the colour to black.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can. Could you mark which building is 22nd December building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put 22 on this building. It's only part of it because it goes all the way to Titova Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could indicate the area of the Markale and the market.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the marketplace is within this quadrant, like this. This is the passage between the building 22 December and the marketplace itself where the stalls are located. So I can mark it with the words "green market."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this. Mr. Karadzic, I take it you're almost finished your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have reduced the scope of the questions that I intended to ask of Mr. Sabljica with regard to Markale. We shall have other witnesses to testify about Markale, but I would like to ask Mr. Sabljica this:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For example, Mr. Sabljica, why you and the other colleague of yours were not on the team the following day.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already answered that, Mr. Karadzic. They did not call us again because there -- it was deemed that we had finished our police task by that time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this sketch been admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D766.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 10455.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who made this sketch that has now just been removed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done by Berko Zecevic, and you asked me if I recognised it as such. I said that I don't know whether it was done by him, but the measurements and the angles are identical to the ones that we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much longer do you need, Mr. Karadzic? Your time is up some time ago.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that if I really do my best, I can finish within the next 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, all these questions put to the witness could be done with another witness. I think you can conclude by 10.00. Conclude by 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, this sketch was made by whom?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it was done by Berko Zecevic. That's what you asked me. When you asked me if it was him, I said that I didn't know. All I can say, that it was a rather precise sketch. It includes the angles and the features identical to the ones that I included in my sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see these stalls in the bottom part?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that the stalls are 0.76 centimetres [as interpreted] and 1.5 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they're identical to the ones that you made?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that identical to the actual stall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we measured the height and the width of the stall on the spot with a measuring tape. They should be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 09620.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Gaynor, I would like you to check if we have the correct English page. The page you indicated is a translation of -- of Mr. Sabljica's drawing, not Mr. Zecevic's drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. We'll check that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1709.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 6 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is the photo file prepared by Sead Besic, the scene of crime officer who was on the spot and who was a member of the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at page 6. How do you explain the difference in the shape of the stall that you portrayed in the sketch of the site and the actual shape of the stall that we can see on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to mark the sizes with a pen on this black and white photograph, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We collapse the English page. We don't need the one. We zoom into the picture once again. We don't need the caption.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But if it's made brighter, it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem. I can use this one, I just want to show you the sizes. So the height of the stall measuring from the ground level up to the top of its roof was 2.1 metres, and the width from the lateral view was 76 centimetres. So this is a lateral view. And this may have confused you because it makes the stall look narrower. I hope this is more clear now. Shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think we have enough markings. All we need is your signature along with the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you have the height and the width of the stall viewed laterally, because with respect to where the shell fell, the wider side was facing Titova Street, and this is identical to the sketch that both Zecevic and I made. I just want to make it clear that this is not a small stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the roof is wider than the working surface of the stall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is extended 5 centimetres on both sides to protect the vendor from rain, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know the size of the roof of the stall?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you add 10 centimetres, 5 on each side, that would make it 86 centimetres, because the working surface is 76 centimetres. These are standard stalls that are used in all marketplaces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, what do we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see the general view of the place where the 120-millimetre shell fell. We see scattered items and produce. We can see blood. We can see broken stalls. That's, I think, what one can see in this photograph. I may have missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted, and then if we can have 65 ter 09620, page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be Exhibit D767.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we need the same document as before, but we'll only just move out a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- no. That's a different photograph. Let's say that we can use this photograph nevertheless. What can one see in this photograph? This is determined in the direction by applying the method that has already been explained. This method should be analysed. Can you tell me, does the right stick has to go upwards, the left has to go downwards in order to determine the direction? Can you please tell me, what can you deduce from this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not understanding what you're saying at all. What do you mean left or right? This is just a close-up of the crater, and this white strip indicates the direction from which the shell came. The traces were so dispersed along the poles of the narrower ellipse so that we only had this position, similar to letter T. So if we look at it in perspective, I think that it's self-explanatory, because the methodology has already been explained in detail as well as by other experts who are dealing with this type of projectile when they want to determine the direction and the orientation. I don't know what you find incomprehensible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is an omission. The witness said 180 degrees, so this should be included in the record, or maybe we can ask the witness to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the angle formed by the traces from the flank from the radial. This is not the deviation angle from the north. That angle was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the last angle, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It refers to the angle reached by connecting ultimate poles of the longer part of the ellipsis which then, in this particular case, forms a 180-degree angle, and in the drawing and by using the compass, it grows out to be 18 degrees north-north-east, or 320 mils.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again with your leave, a general question. Can we have page 6 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you please --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the one. Yes. Can we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the view from Titova Street, from the south to the north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not able to confirm that judging by this photograph. I can't see clearly. I think that this was viewed from the 22nd December building. There might be some caption saying where the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark in this photograph the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I can't see it. I tried to find it, but this photograph is not clear enough. It shows just a general view of the situation that we found at Markale marketplace immediately after the casualties were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the casualties were removed, was any medical analysis or forensic analysis carried out of the site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the coroner's and other forensic experts investigating the wounds and other damage to the casualties? No. That was done at the Kosevo Hospital, because the situation was chaotic. People were brought in in all kinds of vehicles, including trucks, because that was a total massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to your opinion, can anyone mark anything in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, anything that could be relevant for the point of impact and determination of some technical parameters, it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you as an honest professional, Mr. Sabljica. On the assumption that you believe in the same principles, namely that those ethnic groups there should reconcile mutually, would it be better for them to reconcile this year or next year?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I regret it very much that they were ever at war. As a person who considers himself a Bosnian, I see all those peoples as one, and would I like my homeland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all the people who live in it to live a life of prosperity, to become a part of Europe. Regardless of our ethnic differences, I believe we have so much in common that with a little more goodwill we could make much more progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that an erroneously established situation after any incident and false blaming of one or another party would make -- push that reconciliation further away and make it more difficult to restore peace?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speculation on the part of the witness is not helpful. It's not for the witness to answer the question. I take it you conclude your cross-examination. Before we further go on, I have to ask how -- how you are feeling, Mr. Karadzic. Before I entered the courtroom, I was advised that you were not feeling well, and the court deputy observed that you are from time to time dozing. You seem to feel drowsy. How are you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's residual from that cold that I had, but I thought Mr. Sabljica should not be kept waiting, because just a few questions remain till we clear this up, and I believe I can get better. I think, among other things, that this courtroom is a bit colder than it should be, because I have to make an effort three times an hour and a half, like mongoose and cobras I remain immobile. I have to be very focused and I'm fighting for time, and then I suffer back pain and muscle pain that I have to deal with somehow. That's all. Well, the first and obvious thing to do is to see whether this room temperature is adequate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that the Registry is looking into the matter. So I take it that you conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to my time-tested custom, I think I was interrupted, because I think we could have elicited much more professional and unbiased knowledge from this witness. I thank him for his co-operation, and my questions were not unguided missiles. They were more in the spirit of believing that it is the duty of all of us to ensure that reconciliation occurs this year, not next year, not in a decade. And for that reason, Mr. Sabljica, thank you for the effort you invested, and it would be very good if we all invested more efforts to clear up everything that is unclear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'm going to ask you a few questions which arose out of the cross-examination. The first subject I'm going to turn to is the question of sniper nests. Now, for the benefit of the other participants, at page 7707, on the 11th of October, the transcript, Mr. Sabljica, refers to some questions from Mr. Karadzic. He asked you: "Do you recall when Grbavica was reintegrated, as you put it, when we handed Grbavica over to you? "A. I think that was at the end of February or beginning of March 1996. "Q. You said here that in these skyscrapers, one of the four, you had found something that would correspond to sniper nests; right? "A. That's right." Just stopping there for a moment, was it just one of the four skyscrapers that you found something that would correspond to sniper nests?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I was clear enough. All of these four could have been it. We did not look at every apartment, but we looked at all floors upwards of ten in all the four skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, at page 7709, Mr. Karadzic asked you: "Was that dealt with? I mean, the crime scene. Was it dealt with properly? Were photographs taken, et cetera? "A. I'm sure, but I never saw this. I asked why not, but I never received any information in this regard." Later on Mr. Karadzic asked you: "Was this photographed?" And you said: "Yes." And then Mr. Karadzic asked: "Do you -- do we have them?" Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. But I don't have these photographs. If I had, I would have turned them over to the authorities. I was just a member of the team which did that police work. I was an employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. You've --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And still am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've brought us on to the next set of documents. Could I ask for 65 ter 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just before we move on. How long would you expect your redirect to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It should last approximately 45 minutes. That's an approximation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I suggest to have a break now, and the technician will take a look into the temperature matters. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before we adjourn I would like to raise one scheduling matter. This was to some extent foreshadowed earlier. That is Mr. Hamill. The Court will recall we were concerned a bit about his schedule. Mr. Robinson graciously suggested that perhaps it would be better --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not to stop him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, and I think where we are today, it seems clear that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think we'll hear him this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that regard if we have permission to allow the witness to leave. I understand it would actually be helpful for him to get back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will have a break for half an hour. We'll break for half an hour and resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I wanted to ask the Chamber if it would be possible to recess after the re-direct examination because Dr. Karadzic is not feeling well and, frankly, I'm observing that he seems under the effects of the medication and really isn't very with it this morning. So I think it would be better for everyone if he was allowed to go back and rest at the detention unit after this witness completes his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I ask, Mr. Robinson and Mr. Karadzic, this: I raise this just in case. I understand, and I agree that every witness is important, however, given the fact that the next witness will be covering only a limited part, I would like to inquire of you whether it's agreeable to the Defence that the next witness would be cross-examined by one of the legal advisors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I think -- I appreciate that, but for one thing, myself, I'm not in a position to do that because all the preparation is in B/C/S, and also as a matter of principle, Dr. Karadzic's right to self-representation doesn't include that, and we prefer that he cross-examine all of the witnesses. But honestly, he's in no shape to do that. So I'm sorry about that, but I don't think that that would be a feasible alternative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In case an accused is represented and lead counsel is indisposed, the co-counsel may and should be able to lead or cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there's the right to be present, for an accused to be present at his trial. If he's not fit to be even present, then even the lead counsel, co-counsel, or anybody doesn't proceed in his absence without his consent. But I'm not his co-counsel, and he's made it clear that he retains the right to represent himself, so the situation is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: It's one of the anomalies of self-representation, isn't it, Mr. Robinson, that if somebody is represented by counsel they almost inevitably have co-counsel. Where somebody self-represents, although they are deemed to be counsel, there is nobody deemed to be co-counsel. I don't know if that's something that could be remedied in the future, but at the moment that seems to be the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's a real burden on the accused, actually, not to have the assistance of someone who could spell him from time to time. But would I note that in the Tolimir case the Trial Chamber was seized of a request by the legal -- or by Tolimir to allow his legal advisor to conduct some cross-examination from time to time, and they rejected that as incompatible with the self-representation of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was not raising that issue as a matter of principle but whether it could be done on an exceptional basis temporarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: It may be from time to time, with the consent of Dr. Karadzic, that could be done, but in this particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking whether he could consent to that today, but I think I heard the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: If I could also just give you another practical reason beside the principled one, and that is that the preparation for this next witness is entirely in B/C/S by our expert who doesn't speak English and I don't have a familiarity with the material to even be able to do it if Dr. Karadzic was willing to let me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm just raising this hypothetically. What about tomorrow's hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think we should keep that hearing scheduled, and hopefully Dr. Karadzic will be feeling better. I'm also prepared to assist him in that hearing so hopefully we can go forward, but if tomorrow morning he's not able to appear I think the inconvenience would be somewhat minimal because the ambassador -- the representative of the Government of Bosnia, the ambassador, is here full-time in the Netherlands, so if we have to postpone the hearing at the last minute, it won't be much of inconvenience to anyone, I don't think. So I think we should try to conduct that hearing as scheduled and if tomorrow morning the situation is different, we can reassess at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any observation to make, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me refrain from broad propositions with respect to the numerous issues raised by the Court, most of which we support and encourage, but I think in this particular situation, obviously the Court's facing a decision about an immediate balance of interest, and I presume what the Court was interested in knowing was whether or not a postponement of this witness's testimony presents some extraordinary logistical implications that the Court needs to be aware of immediately. In that regard, anticipating this possibility, we did raise this issue at the break. I understand that, while clearly not convenient and the witness has been here for some period of time, there are not circumstances which prevent his return or make it so inconvenient that it's an impossibility. So it's matter of balancing the relative interest but there is no particular extraordinary circumstance that I need bring the Court's attention to that would militate dramatically in favour of insistence that we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Let's proceed your -- with your re-examination, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I continue, I simply want to note for the record a page reference which you asked me to provide earlier, and the English translation of the sketch by Mr. Zecevic of the Markale I incident appears at page 4 of the English version of 65 ter 10676.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, as you recall, before the break we were discussing the subject of sniper incidents, and I was just about to call up document 22983, please. Mr. Sabljica, when these documents arrive, you will see that they are a series of 11 investigative reports. Most of them are one page long. And if we can just focus on the very first one. If we just zoom in a little bit. Almost all of the reports are in very much identical format with slightly different details in each of them. This report is dated the 25th of April of 1996. Mr. Sabljica, you see you're named as number 3 in the participants in this investigation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's my name under number 3, ballistics expert from the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And the introductory part refers to the discovery of a sniper nest at the 13th floor of the skyscraper at number 6A Grbavicka Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Before it was renamed Grbavicka street it was Lenjinova Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lenin Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In the final paragraph of this, which is on the next page in the English version, it's on this page in the original, in the final sentence we see the words: "In the room, some 20 bullet cases were found which the ballistics expert established to be of 7.9 millimetre calibre, and some 10 bullet cases of 7.62 millimetre calibre." Do you recall your participation in this investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's part of this investigation that I explained when we toured the skyscrapers. So I confirm and I know that Mr. Enes Zeljkovic, who was a member of the team, collected this evidence and photographed it, as written here. The site was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we go to the next page of this document in B/C/S and in English, please. This document is, I think it's fair to say, in almost identical format to the first document, and it refers to the 13th floor of the skyscraper at number 6A Grbavicka Street. This time it's apartment 52. The first document referred to apartment 51. And a sniper nest was found there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's a reference further down the document to the discovery of 20 bullet cases which the ballistics expert established to be of 7.9 millimetre calibre. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I don't propose to take you through each and every one of these, but I would like to move to one of the documents refers to location at number 2A Rave Jankovica Street, the 18th floor of that building. That's the second last document in B/C/S, please. And it's the seventh the page from the end in the English version. Mr. Sabljica, this refers to an investigation on the following date, the 26th of April, 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again we see a reference to the discovery of bullet cases for 7.9 and 7.62 millimetre calibre. Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's written here. Late Medjedovic and I were on the team as ballistics experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In the next document, please, which also dates from the 26th of April, 1996, we see a reference to a similar investigation. In this case you're listed as participant number 4, and the location is the ground floor of 26 Grbavicka Street. Apologies, the location of this place is 45 Smederevska Street.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smederevska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. You can recall the locations of the two streets we've just looked at, can you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask -- before we go on, could I ask that this 65 ter be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1736, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd request the registrar to bring up Exhibit P1724.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you remember marking this map earlier in your evidence, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Are the four skyscrapers marked with the figure 1, those are the four skyscrapers on Grbavicka Street, formerly known as Lenjinova Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you be able to mark for the Court where Ravje Jankovic street is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we use a blue pen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we zoom in a bit on the lower left corner. Ravje Jankovic Street used to begin here and continued into Grbavica. And the skyscraper, I know exactly where it is; my late sister used to live there. That's the building I'm talking about. Which number do you want me to mark it with?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If you could mark it with number 6, please. In the report we've just looked at we saw the discovery of a sniper nest at the 18th floor of that building. Do you happen to know how many floors it has in total?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eighteen, I think. It has also attic premises on the top, like storage space for residents who live upwards of the 10th floor. I think the 18th floor is the last floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Gaynor. Mr. Karadzic, I forgot to ask whether the temperature now suits you now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's a little better, and I also put something on under my jacket, but I believe it's better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I want to tell you that you may be excused if you wish, on the understanding that Mr. Robinson will look after your interest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but we'll stay together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Sabljica, does Smederevska Street appear on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smederevska Street is in Vraca. I don't know what it's called now. You can't see it on this view. It's further to the south. It's a private house in the neighbourhood of Vraca where we conducted an on-site investigation, but that was an anti-aircraft gun, machine-gun, 12.7 millimetres, and that machine-gun covered both military sections held by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the streets starting from the intersection with the railway hotel, the Bolnicka Street, the whole part up to the Vrbanja Bridge, and that machine-gun had a very good overview. It was a heavy weapon, not an infantry weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that this be admitted, the -- the marked-up photograph, either under the same P number or as Your Honours wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to give a separate number because we changed the format. We'll give a separate number. Ah. Could you put the date again, because the date is different, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1737.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could I now ask for 65 ter 22982, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What will appear on your screen in a moment, Mr. Sabljica, is a set of a number of photo documentation files. Again I'm not going to take the Court through every single photograph, I simply want to ask you, Mr. Sabljica, to perhaps explain a couple of them to us. First of all, if you could look at the front of this. We don't actually have an English translation yet. Could you just read out the location of this and the subject of this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Photo documentation. Case: Discovery of a number of sniper emplacements. Place: Sarajevo, Grbavicka Street, numbers 8 through -- we cannot see -- formerly Lenin Street. Date of photographs: 25th April, 1996, 13 photographs."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we go to page 5, please. Could you explain what we're looking at there, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we see the view from that place through the hole, as the scenes of crime officer wrote below, showing the zone of action directed at Holiday Inn Hotel, and you can see the hotel in the distance through the opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we go to page 7, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again could you briefly explain what this picture shows.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It used to be a bedroom in the north-west wing of the building. The opening is of dimensions 20 X 20 centimetres on the northern and western walls of the bedroom, protected by sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Again, just briefly tell us what this photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Casings of 7.62 and 7.9 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: These were found in this location as part of this investigation. Is that what we are to understand?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the next picture that gives another aspect of this site.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just briefly tell us what that is, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the view through the opening on the northern wall of the room, showing the area of activity in the direction of the KMT. You can see the railroad -- sorry, the tram tracks in the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That was page 9. Could we now have page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Tell us briefly what you see there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: View through the opening on the western wall of the room, showing the activity on Zmaja od Bosne Street, the former Putnik building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I have page 14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do you see in this photograph, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: View through the said opening, showing the area of activity in the direction of the tram stop Technical School.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's the end of that file. If we just go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are going along, Mr. Gaynor, I was wondering why we didn't see these pictures during your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's a fair question, Your Honour. These were not part of Mr. Sabljica's earlier evidence when he previously testified before the Tribunal. Mr. Karadzic expressly asked if there were photographs. He asked does the witness have them, do we have them. That was part of the reason which impelled me to try to find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I mean, I -- I was sitting, waiting to see if there was going to be an objection from the Defence but made the assumption there wasn't objection because it was not objected that they should appear in evidence. So that clears up that mystery. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, again if you just briefly describe what this particular file depicts. Sorry, what the title says, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Photo documentation. Case: Discovery of sniper nests. Place: Sarajevo Grbavicka 6A street, formerly Lenin Street. Date of photography: 25 April 1996. 16 photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Finally, we'll just turn to the 6th page of this file, please, which should be about page 21. What do we see there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: View through the right-hand opening on the northern wall of the room, showing the area of activity in the direction of the tram stop Technical School.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In fact, if we could see the photograph prior to that one, please, as well. That will do. If you could explain what that is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The side wall of the bedroom, with the visible opening 30 X 30 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, the rest of these photographs are of similar nature. I propose to tender this set of photographs now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, we'll admit it. Do we need the translation of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I suppose the translation of -- of the description of each photograph would be useful, so we can request that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll mark it --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- for identification, pending translation of that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P1738.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As the next subject, Mr. Sabljica, I'd like you to clear up the orientation of a map which -- of a sketch of a crime scene. This is a sketch of the crime scene for incident G7, which Mr. Karadzic questioned you about. And first of all, I'd like to bring up 65 ter 13581, please. Now, if you look at the green dot marked 7 on this map, Mr. Sabljica, do you -- do you accept that that marks approximately the midpoint between the three shells which landed on the 4th of February, 1994, in the incident which was located near to Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what's written here, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask that this be admitted as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, that's page 10 of the Sarajevo-specific court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1739.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I now ask for 65 ter 22986, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, do you think you'd be able to mark the street Oslobodilaca Sarajeva on this map? I should say on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try, but I'm not 100 per cent certain. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can return to the previous map, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or -- he --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- hard copy of page 10 of this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm wondering what the value is of him simply copying from one map to another. This seems like the kind of thing that you would say Dr. Karadzic is wasting time on. If all he's doing is copying from one map to another, we can all do that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not really. I don't see any problem, the witness being assisted by the map he just saw a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have found the street and now I can mark it. It's this street over here. The place of the incident was here. Actually, this playground. Oslobodilaca Sarajeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And just mark the figure 1 where you suggest the incident was.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could sign and date that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, could we just -- just zoom in on location of the street for a moment so the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give the number for this. Exhibit P1740.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After keeping them, we'll zoom in further. No, we use the kept one. Use P1740.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, does that -- does that refresh your memory sufficiently well of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Would you like me to mark it here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As it's -- as it's already marked, I think we can move on to -- to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the -- some confusion arose yesterday as to the -- the depiction of the direction north on a sketch relating to this incident. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you that sketch, and it's been reoriented in direction, and I want you to have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So could I ask for 09617A, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give the number again?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It was 09617A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has it been released?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can come back to that. Sorry. I think it should be all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. On my -- my computer. Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this sketch you can see all of the words you saw yesterday are in fact upside-down, but could we just keep the orientation that it was -- could we keep the orientation with the words upside-down. Thank you very much. It might be slightly unusual orientation for you, Mr. Sabljica, but can you -- can you comment as to whether this, in fact, agrees with the incident location if we were to suggest that the cardinal points of the compass were north going straight up?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps two or three degrees more in terms of an acute angle. Can I draw that? Two or three degrees. This is a segment of that street now, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva. So may I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. And if you need the assistance of the photograph or any maps, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps the north should be here a bit. I'm going to mark it as north. Because the street runs this way and -- it's not quite vertical. Had you rotated this a bit more, say 5 degrees, instead of having it perpendicular in relation to the street. Had you rotated the photograph, say by 5 degrees, it would have been more precise in relation to the map that I marked a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You're -- you're satisfied that the direction you've marked as north is -- is your calculation of where north should be. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Fine. If you could just sign and date that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd ask that that be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1741.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, my final question in fact just concerns the record of the proceedings. If you could just help me with the one small thing. This was at page 7780. Mr. Karadzic said to you -- said to the Court, he said: "This was the city plan for the city of Sarajevo issued by, published by Slovenes, and on the back of the plan there is a whole list of new and old names." A few lines later, he said: "Well, I think we now have the original document. Can I please ask the usher's assistance. Well, let me just take a look at it and we'll show it to the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber." That's the end of that extract. I'd just like to show you the back of that particular map for a moment. Mr. Sabljica, if you could open the map and direct your attention to the box on the right-hand part of the map, indicating who produced the map. Could you just tell the Court who produced the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: CIP, "Narodna Biblioteka Srbije," that is the National Library of Serbia, Belgrade, Catalogue. Should I read it on?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue to the actual company, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sarajevo Plan Grada," city map. Editor: Goran Jovanovic. 1:20000 is the scale, Info System Fotografija 2005 Belgrade. One geographic map."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's fine, thank you. And can you help me on another point: Is there a list of new and old names on the back of that map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to take a look. No. I think only the new names of streets are registered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Sabljica, that concludes your evidence here today, and on behalf of the Bench and the Tribunal, I thank you for your coming to The Hague again to give it. Now you are free to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Sabljica. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Defence please ask the witness to identify on Google the situation as it is, in order to do away with any possible dilemmas in this regard? Could we please have 65 ter 22986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your point of question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm afraid -- actually, I think we need to identify this. And also, there are many other minor points which seem to have been elucidated but actually there is a confusion in terms of the otherwise simple picture of the situation on the ground and cardinal points, and that is going to constitute a major problem. On the image of the garage, on this one example, we can show what this looks like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Usually Defence is not allowed to ask question -- further cross-examination unless a new item has been triggered, arose during the redirect examination. Mr. Gaynor, what -- do you have any observation to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If it arises directly out of the redirect and couldn't reasonably have been foreseen, I've no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not object to his further cross-examination in relation to that sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I do not object. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. One further question, Mr. Sabljica. So shall we bring up the P exhibit, P1741.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this Google image, can you mark the garage?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom in a bit, the area where Oslobodilaca Sarajeva is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We did it. Why don't we let him compare two -- two image, one Google image and the other the sketch. So why don't we bring up two images, one being P1740, the other P1741.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have this Google image on one part of the screen and then the sketch where the garage is marked -- or, rather, the first impact, could we have that on the other part.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just so the record is absolutely accurate, the satellite image we're looking at is not actually Google maps. In this instance it was shot by the satellite Quick Bird in October 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is the image we need the one we see on the left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's coming.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you look at these two images, that is to say the image and the sketch, and could you mark your knowledge on both, what it is that you had established.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The garage should be in this upper part of the playground, somewhere around here. That's where the garage should be, because you see it here. It's along the entire length of the playground. There is a building, there is a passageway here, and then you get there according to this angle. I told you that if the streets were to be rotated -- that is where the garage was. And this is the playground here. See, here. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We do not see what you're indicating. I'm afraid that we cannot see that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I marked with red, that's where the garage should be, along that. And perpendicular to the garage is the building. You see it. You see it on the drawing, don't you, along with the blue line where I marked the street. You can see it on the map as well. That's it. That's how I see it on the basis of this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I remind you, what is this in the corner? It is the runway, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Dobrinja, in a way, is parallel to the airport, and most of its streets are either parallel or perpendicular to the airport; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The north is as you had decided last time. So these streets are about 10 or 15 minutes; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that are perpendicular to the airport move towards the south-west/north-east in relation to the airport. They do not fully coincide with the north. So there is that slight difference, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the south-east and north-west actually?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I'm going to draw the north for you here in relation to Oslobodilaca Sarajeva. I'm using a different colour. Actually, I'm using red now. I'll draw it here. This is north. And you see how the streets run.
