utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can go on, if you wish, through the built-up area to the airport.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's north, here's south. [In English] East, west. [Interpretation] In relation to the street; right? So this is an idealised picture. Had they turned this image a bit further you will see on the drawing, around the satellite image the streets are not parallel, part of the streets on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva. The sketch should be turned to the left a bit more and then the directions would coincide with what I drew on the satellite image. You have it here in the corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether it's possible, but could you draw a line on the sketch which is on the right side, indicating the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, if my pronunciation is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the street Oslobodilaca Sarajeva, OS. You can see it here. And the north is here, in this direction. Now, if we were to rotate this map a bit -- or, rather, the sketch, then it would be parallel to the blue line Oslobodilaca Sarajeva in relation to this one marked here, so then this would fully coincide. It is very hard to draw on this kind of sketch that just shows a segment of the scene or site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the street runs in the direction to the north-east, rather, mildly.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: South-west/north-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now use the blue marker to mark these 20 or 15 degrees in terms of how it diverges from the north as such.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to extend it, this would be the angle; right? Let's call it Alpha. I'm going to extend the north as well so you have a better picture of it. It's not that precise now, but approximately. I mean, it's hard to draw this thing through maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And whether you can indicate that degree -- Alpha degree on the right side sketch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. This is where the Alpha angle would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We made a mistake, tendered a different map. We have a Slovenian map as well. However there is no difference whatsoever in view of those elements that we are concerned with. So if there is any dilemma, if you'd like this map to be obtained as well, the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, could you kindly put the date and your signature on this image.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be given a separate D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D768.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I notice you rose, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Simply to say that we would -- we would be happy to receive a copy of the Slovenian map so we could verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That has concluded your cross -- further cross-examination. Dr. Subotic is saying yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like Mr. Sabljica to sign the sketch as well. That might be useful too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's signed, and it says the 14th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But with the new markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's kept all together. We'll save the image all together in one image. I think that was done. Can I confirm with the court deputy? Yes. This is what we saved.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to assure Mr. Sabljica, as I hope he has seen for himself, that I have been dealing with this material in the work of different groups. I'm not doing anything on a personal level in terms of the members of these groups. I would like to establish that we are both in favour of the reconciliation of the people down there, and it's better if it takes place today rather than tomorrow, and this reconciliation is going to happen if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not necessary to make a statement here. So that concludes, really, your evidence, thank you again, and now you're free to go, Mr. Sabljica. So we'll -- just wait. We'll draw the curtain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's one matter I'd like to deal with very briefly in private session. Shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On 28th of September, 2010, Mr. Karadzic raised the issue of a possible site visit by the Chamber to a particular location in Sarajevo. Treating this as a form of oral motion for a site visit, the Chamber asked the parties to make written submissions, which were received on 6th and 7th October 2010. Having considered those submissions, the Chamber does not consider it to be seized of a motion for a site visit at this stage. However, we wish to inform the parties that we are of the view that a site visit to certain locations in and around Sarajevo may indeed be helpful and that this is something which the Chamber is contemplating for the future. The parties should bear in mind that organisation of a site visit requires significant advance planning in the region of at least three months and that this needs to be taken into account should they wish to make a motion for a site visit. Should no such motion be filed, the Chamber will raise the matter again at least three months before the anticipated end of the Prosecution 's case. We reiterate that, for security reasons, it is important for all such discussions to be conducted in private session or on a confidential basis, and for that reason we deny Mr. Karadzic's request for his submission to be reclassified as a public document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Would the Chamber be minded to make more than one site visit so that it would see the sites of Sarajevo on one occasion and then later on would make another visit, if necessary, to other parts of Bosnia? Because our concern in making the motion was that we're not in a position to suggest locations outside of Sarajevo, but we are in a position to suggest locations within Sarajevo, and we didn't think that the Chamber would otherwise be minded to make more than one site visit; but if you are, then we can make that motion with respect to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are free to make any submission which you would find helpful, but it relates to some certain budgetary and financial problem, but we may consider whatever submission you make. Shall we go back to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of the health condition of the accused, we find it inappropriate and impractical to continue today. We'll adjourn for today, and we'll resume tomorrow at 10.00 for a hearing which relates to Bosnia binding order. We'll rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 15th day of October, 2010, at 10.00 a.m.
